summary: Willard Van Orman Quine was a philosopher and linguist who studied at Oberlin College (1926–1930) and Harvard University (1930–1932). He served in the U.S. Navy (1942–1945) and held posts at Wesleyan University (1964–1965) and Harvard (1933–1978).

Willem Bollée was an Indologist who studied at Utrecht University (c. 1947–1956) and the University of Hamburg (c. 1965–1975). He was an assistant professor at the University of Münster (1971–1978) and taught at Heidelberg University (professor from 1979).

Willem Caland was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Leiden University (c. 1877–1882). He held posts at Leiden (1913–1914) and Utrecht University, where he held the Chair of Sanskrit (c. 1903–1929) and served as Professor of Sanskrit (1906–1917).

Willem van der Molen is a scholar of linguistics, history, archaeology, and Indology who studied at Leiden University (c. 1971–1983). He held posts at Leiden University (c. 1979–2017) and the University of Indonesia.
William C. Kirby is a sinologist and historian who studied at Dartmouth College (c. 1968–1972) and Harvard University (c. 1972–1981). He held a post at Harvard University starting around 1992.

William Carey was an Indologist and linguist who studied under traditional teacher Golok Nath Sharma. He founded the Serampore Mission Press and served as Professor of Sanscrit, &c. at Fort William College in 1801.
William Chu is a scholar in Buddhist studies who completed his MA at the University of California, Los Angeles by 2006 and studied under doctoral supervisor Robert E. Buswell Jr.

William Dwight Whitney, an Indologist and linguist, studied at Williams, Yale, Berlin, and Tübingen under Salisbury, Weber, von Roth, and Bopp. He was a professor of Sanskrit at Yale (1853–1894) and served in the American Oriental Society.

William Edelglass is a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies. He has taught philosophy at Colby College (attested 2007) and held positions at Marlboro College (attested 2013) and the Institute of Buddhist Dialectics.
William Erskine was a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology. He was educated at the Royal High School and studied at the University of Edinburgh from around 1787 to 1792.
William Frederic Sinclair was a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology who studied at the Royal School, Armagh. He held a post in the Indian Civil Service beginning in 1866.

William H. Nienhauser, Jr. is a sinologist who studied at Indiana University (c. 1968–1972) under Irving Yucheng Lo and Friedrich Alexander Bischoff, and at the University of Bonn. He joined the University of Wisconsin-Madison faculty around 1972.
William J. Johnson is a scholar in Indology and religious studies who held posts at Cardiff University and the University of Wales (attested 1998).

William James was a scholar of philosophy and religious studies who studied at Plymouth College and Harvard University, including its School of Engineering and Medical School (c. 1861–1869). He held a post at Harvard from around 1872 to 1907.

William Jones was an Indologist and linguist educated at Harrow School and University College, Oxford (c. 1764–1768). He became Chief Justice of the Supreme Court of Judicature at Fort William in 1783 and founded the Asiatic Society in 1784.

William L. Ames is a scholar in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. He studied at Caltech and the University of Washington under Collett Cox and David Seyfort Ruegg, and held posts at Washington, CIIS, and JFK University.

William L. Smith is an Indologist who held academic posts at Stockholm University (c. 1980–2007), the University of Wisconsin-Madison, and Hampton University, as well as a post at the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration.

William M. Bodiford is a Buddhist studies and Japanology scholar who studied at Kansas, Tsukuba, Komazawa, and Yale. He held posts at Meiji Gakuin, the University of Iowa, and UCLA, where he became a professor around 1992.

William M. Gorvine is a scholar of Tibetology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Connecticut College and the University of Virginia, completing his PhD under David Germano in 2006.

William Magee is a Tibetologist and Buddhist studies scholar who earned his PhD at the University of Virginia under Jeffrey Hopkins. He held posts at Virginia, Dharma Drum Buddhist College, and the Chung-Hwa Institute of Buddhist Studies.
